prompt: Nowadays the way many people interact with each other has changed because of technology. In what ways has technology affected the types of relationships that people make? Has this been a positive or negative development?
essay:
Technology has transformed the way people communicate, and this has significantly changed the kinds of relationships they form. While it has made social connections wider and more convenient, I believe this development is mainly positive, provided that online interaction does not completely replace face-to-face communication.

One major effect of technology is that people can now build relationships beyond their immediate surroundings. In the past, friendships were usually formed at school, work, or within the local community. Today, social media, messaging applications, and video calls allow individuals to maintain contact with people across different cities and countries. For example, international students can keep close relationships with their families while also forming new friendships online with people who share similar interests.

Technology has also changed professional relationships. Many workers now collaborate with colleagues they may rarely or never meet in person. Online platforms have made remote teamwork, international business partnerships, and digital networking much more common. This can create valuable opportunities, especially for people living in smaller towns or developing countries, because they are no longer limited by geography.

However, there are some drawbacks. Online relationships can sometimes be shallow, and people may present idealised versions of themselves on social media. In addition, excessive reliance on digital communication may reduce people’s ability to develop deeper emotional bonds through direct conversation, body language, and shared experiences. Despite this, these problems are not caused by technology itself, but by how people use it.

In conclusion, technology has expanded personal and professional relationships by making communication faster, easier, and more global. Although it can weaken genuine connection if overused, I believe it is generally a positive development when balanced with real-life interaction.
